design.environment: 3x3 gridworld; state {x,y}; actions up/down/left/right; goal (2,2); boundary bumps; 20% perpendicular slide

reward.note: bump reward includes the step penalty: -1 step and -2 bump penalty

stochasticity.rule: a slipped action executes one of the two perpendicular directions with equal probability; out-of-bounds remains in place

policies.greedy: Manhattan shortest-path direction on the known deterministic grid, replanned after every observed position
policies.pomdp: package POMDPPlanner.plan with ParticleFilter and QMDPSolver; no observations are supplied, so the belief is only predicted, never corrected

trials.starts: the same 20 start cells (drawn with replacement from the 8 non-goal cells) are used by all policies in every repetition

rule: add-opt-in iff [pomdp.successRate >= greedy.successRate + 0.10 OR pomdp.successRate >= random.successRate + 0.20] AND pomdp.avgPlanMs < 500 AND successVarianceAcrossRepetitions <= 0.15; otherwise do-not-add
decisionInterpretation: POMDP does not beat the greedy baseline by 0.10 (delta 0.000); the add-opt-in decision is driven by the random-policy branch (delta 0.430) plus the time and variance checks.

successVariance.note: sample variance (n-1 denominator) of the 5 per-repetition success rates; trial-level Bernoulli variance p*(1-p) is also included in each aggregate

limitations: the package uses Math.random internally, so POMDP planning is not seed-reproducible; only the baselines use a seeded PRNG
POMDPPlanner is called without observations, so the particle filter never corrects its belief; particles are only propagated through the stochastic transition
the rollout policy inside QMDPSolver is greedy on immediate reward with 10% random exploration; it is an approximation, not an exact POMDP solve
the state is effectively observed by the planner via the sampled nextState, which is optimistic relative to a true partially observable setting
the 3x3 grid is small and all 20 starts must reuse the 8 non-goal cells
success variance is estimated from only 5 repetition rates, so it is coarse
planDurationMs is measured by the package with Date.now (millisecond resolution)

the package uses Math.random internally, so average plan time is not reproducible across executions; the average can hide a heavy tail (individual plans in this class of run can exceed 500ms even when the mean is below it)
